data.one_liner: A GraphQL client for Flutter with widget wrappers and hooks.
data.what_it_does: Provides an idiomatic Flutter API, widgets, and hooks to execute GraphQL queries, mutations, and subscriptions. It supports caching, optimistic UI updates, and pagination out of the box.
use_when: You are building a Flutter app that communicates with a GraphQL backend.
You want declarative Query and Mutation widgets or hooks in your UI.
avoid_when: Your backend uses a standard REST API instead of GraphQL.
You prefer an extremely lightweight HTTP client without schema caching.
strengths: Comprehensive feature set including caching, pagination, and optimistic mutations.
Supports both traditional Flutter widgets and flutter_hooks.
Built-in integration for local persistence stores like Hive.
weaknesses: Requires specific Android build configurations (Java 17 and Gradle 8.4).
Can add substantial complexity for simple applications.
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing Hive for caching, wrapping your app with GraphQLProvider, and updating Android settings to Java 17 and Gradle 8.4.
